Mortgages and deeds of trust with a power of sale may be foreclosed by sale by the mortgagee/trustee without suit; such sales are valid and forever foreclose the equity of redemption of the property sold.
Deeds of trust may be foreclosed by suit or, at the holder's option, by trustee's sale.

Sale notice must be advertised: in counties with a city of 50,000+ in a daily newspaper at least 20 times through the day of sale; in other counties in a weekly paper for four successive issues (or at least once a week for four successive weeks in a daily/triweekly/semiweekly paper).
The notice must set forth the date and book/page of the record, grantors, time, terms and place of sale, and a description of the property.

Foreclosing mortgagee or trustee must mail certified/registered notice at least 20 days before the sale to the record owner as of 40 days before sale, the mortgagor/grantor, and persons who recorded a request for notice.
Trustee sales held between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. are deemed commercially reasonable.

Where the holder or its agent buys at a trustee's sale of a deed of trust, the grantor or heirs/assigns may redeem within one year of the sale by giving written notice at the sale or within ten days before the advertised sale and paying the debt, interest, prior encumbrances, taxes, assessments and costs.

If the property in the affidavit exceeds $15,000, the clerk publishes a creditor notice once a week for two consecutive weeks.
An executor or administrator may petition the court to sell, mortgage or lease real property of the estate; notice of hearing goes to heirs and devisees.
